anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Anomaly Definition: The database simultaneously suffers from (1) application-level statements and transaction patterns that process far more data or hold resources much longer than business logic requires (SQL Workload Logic Anomaly), (2) stale or incomplete optimizer statistics that drive systematic cardinality misestimates and poor plan choices (Optimizer Statistics Anomaly), and (3) heavy blocking and deadlock situations inside the lock manager as concurrent sessions compete for the enlarged lock footprint produced by the first two problems (Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly).

Combined Observable Phenomena: • Extreme and highly variable statement and transaction latencies, with the same SQLs dominating slow-query and deadlock logs. • Execution plans showing gross mismatches between estimated and actual row counts, frequent recompiles after data changes, and sudden plan regressions. • Long blocker–waiter chains, lock-wait time spikes, automatic lock escalation to page or table level, and periodic deadlock victim errors driving application retries. • Connection pools saturate, application threads time out, and overall throughput collapses even while CPU and I/O utilization appear moderate because many sessions are stalled on locks.

Interaction and Causal Chain: Inefficient SQL or over-wide transactions generated by the application touch far more rows than necessary, dramatically inflating the number and scope of locks acquired. Because optimizer statistics are stale or lack correlation information, the engine routinely misestimates cardinalities, often selecting scan-heavy or poorly ordered plans that further expand the data and lock footprint. These oversized, mis-planned operations run longer, block more resources, and trigger lock-escalation or deadlock scenarios. The resulting lock contention feeds back into application behavior—timeouts cause retries, which issue the same inefficient queries again—exacerbating concurrency pressure. Meanwhile, the inflated workloads delay automatic statistics refreshes, keeping the optimizer blind and locking the system into a vicious cycle of bad plans, long transactions, and escalating contention that degrades OLTP performance end-to-end.

entry.official_description: InnoDB: Table %s contains %lu indexes inside InnoDB, which is different from the number of indexes %u defined in MySQL.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
